_comment: Scripts under scripts/ that have NO dedicated python/tests/test_<stem>.py and are ACCEPTED,
each with the reason. scripts/check_script_test_coverage.py fails on any script not listed
here, and equally on any entry here whose script has gone away or has SINCE GAINED a test --
a closed gap left recorded goes on excusing the file, and would silently re-cover it if that
test were later deleted.
WHY THESE SCRIPTS GET A LEDGER AT ALL. They are this repository's invariant enforcement: make
check runs thirty of them and the witnesses job runs twenty-nine. A guard script whose own
behaviour nothing asserts can stop guarding and go on reporting green, which is the failure
python/tests/test_make_check_runs_in_ci.py was written about one level up -- a check that
passes is indistinguishable from a check that is running.
THE MEASURED BASELINE was 11 of 51 scripts, listed with line counts in the checker's own
docstring. This file holds EIGHT, because three of the eleven were closed with real unit tests
in the same change rather than recorded: image_tags.py (test_image_tags.py),
check_image_digests.py (test_check_image_digests.py) and check_cask_stanzas.py
(test_check_cask_stanzas.py). All three are pure logic over a tmp_path fixture with no network
and no Docker, which is what made them the closable three. The ledger therefore ships smaller
than the gap it records, and the direction it is moving is visible rather than asserted.
The Go surface was measured at the same time for comparison and has no structural gap worth
recording: all 27 packages under internal/, pkg/ and cmd/ carry a *_test.go, across 209
non-test source files. This file is the whole of the measured deficit.
`exercised_by` is not an exemption and does not suppress anything on its own -- the reason
does. It is recorded because indirect coverage under another file's name is a materially
different situation from no coverage at all, and a ledger that flattened the two would be
lying in the safe-looking direction. Three entries carry one.
`lines` is the size at the time of recording. It is not checked and is not a contract: it is
there so a reader can see at a glance which of these is worth closing next, the way the
checker's docstring orders its baseline by size. govern_ingest.py at 717 lines is the largest
unguarded surface in this directory by a factor of two and a half.

accepted.reason: The OpenMetadata ingest, and the largest unguarded script here by a wide margin. It is an integration entry point rather than a logic module: every function it exposes talks to a live OpenMetadata server over HTTP or reads a real Delta table, so a unit test would assert against a mock of the API whose shape is the actual risk. Its behaviour is proved end to end by the `governance` and `governance-sso` CI jobs, which stand up OpenMetadata with Postgres and Elasticsearch, run this script, and require OM's own API to return the table with columns mapped from the Delta schema. The pure-logic parts worth pinning have already been LIFTED OUT and are tested: the type mapping by test_check_govern_types.py and the column schema by test_govern_column_schema.py. Closing this properly means continuing that extraction, not adding a mock.

A NAMING MISS, not a coverage gap: python/tests/test_cron_workflow_freshness.py drives this checker directly and is simply missing the `check_` prefix the rule looks for. Recorded rather than renamed because the rename is a separate change with its own diff -- this checker's job is to make the discrepancy visible, and a silent rename in the same commit that introduced the rule would be the rule bending to fit the tree instead of the reverse.

A build-time wheel builder, and what it produces is what proves it: the `fixture-wheels` CI job runs it on every pull request precisely because a tag-only invocation could not fail the change that broke it -- v0.21.0 shipped with no wheels when contoso-fixtures gained a uv path dependency that does not survive into wheel metadata. That job builds the set and resolves it, which is the assertion. A unit test over a stubbed pyproject would re-assert the string handling and could not have caught the defect that motivated the job.

Its one load-bearing claim IS unit-tested, deliberately and separately: the redactor, whose own docstring warns that passing one value through 'publishes a real customer's hostname forever'. That is scripts/check_capture_redaction.py, covered by python/tests/test_check_capture_redaction.py and run by both `make check` and the witnesses job. The rest of this file drives a real tenant from real-fabric.yml's workflow_dispatch and cannot run without one.

A vendoring script whose output is the thing under test, and the output is asserted hard: it refreshes third_party/notebookutils-stubs from Microsoft's own pinned stubs, and scripts/check_notebookutils_surface.py --strict then requires every difference between our shim and those stubs to be allowed and to carry a reason. That runs in `make check` and in the witnesses job. Testing the fetcher rather than the vendored result would assert the download and not the contract.

The same shape as vendor_notebookutils_stubs.py one vocabulary over: it vendors ADF's activity-type table, and scripts/check_adf_activity_types.py holds the emulator's dispatch to what was vendored -- the check that found SparkJob falling to the success stub. The vendored file is reviewed as a diff when it is refreshed, which is the only review a vendoring step can usefully get.

A diagnostic, not an invariant: `make spark` and `sh scripts/status.sh --spark` run it to answer whether a LIVE stack is usable, driving Livy through spark-agent into Sail and reporting what it found. Every branch requires containers, and its subject -- that the Spark path works -- is asserted by the e2e suites that exercise the same chain for real (livy-native, spark-a2, notebook-run). A unit test here would mock the stack whose reachability is the entire question.
exercised_by: ci: livy-native, spark-a2, notebook-run (the same chain, live)

accepted.reason: A one-shot investigation probe, kept as the record of a measurement rather than as a guard: it asks a live Sail whether a premise about MERGE holds. It is in no Makefile target and no workflow, so it enforces nothing and nothing depends on its behaviour. A test would pin the shape of a question already answered. If it ever becomes a gate, it needs a test and this entry has to go.
